newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco tenders for turn-key GSM phone exchange.
newsitem.headline: Morocco tenders for turn-key GSM phone exchange.

text.p: Morocco launched on Monday an international tender for the purchase of a turn-key GSM telephone exchange system, officials said.

"The new equipment is aimed at the commercial and technical management of subscribers to the GSM (Global System for Mobile Telecommunications) mobile telephone system," an official at the state-run Office National des Postes et Telecommunications (ONPT) said.
Subscribers to the tender should deliver a provisional guarantee of 320,000 dirhams ($36,800) before the closing date of November 27, 1996, he said.
The tender coincides with a debate on privatisation of the telecommunication system considered by the opposition "as a strategic sector".
Last week, the government of Prime Minister Abdellatif Filali started examining a draft law which would open telecommunications to the private sector.
South Korean giant Daewoo, the U.S. AT&T and French Alcatel companies have shown interest in Morocco's plan to privatise the GSM mobile telephone system, an official at the finance ministry said.
Morocco has an estimated 30,000 subscribers to the GSM system introduced during the meeting of the General Agreement on Trade and Tariffs (GATT) in Marrakesh in 1994.
Earlier this year, the ONPT announced it would invest $1.5 billion over the next five years to expand and improve the telephone network.
With its 27 million inhabitants, the kingdom has a teledensity of four percent, or four phone lines per 100 inhabitants.
